title: Atomic time-window export snapshots for scheduled and ad-hoc CSV deliveries
creator: Maya O'Connor
description:
Problem: Scheduled CSV and ad-hoc tenant exports currently use eventual consistency windows that can surface partial or overlapping rows when customers request point-in-time downloads or when we perform incremental runs with retries. This causes customer confusion during audits and makes diffs between successive exports noisy.

Goal: Implement an atomic, time-window snapshot mechanism that produces consistent CSV slices for a tenant for an explicit closed time window (e.g., [t0, t1)) that can be produced both on-schedule and on-demand. Snapshots must be resumable, idempotent, and compatible with existing S3/HTTP webhook delivery and ZIP/manifest formats.

Scope:
- Define snapshot anchoring model and metadata fields for manifests (snapshot_id, anchored_at, window_start, window_end, source_checkpoint).
- Provide a lightweight coordinator service to create snapshot manifests and lock impacted partition ranges for the duration of export preparation.
- Enable resumable CSV builders that can rehydrate from a checkpoint and produce identical output even if workers fail and retry.
- Ensure backward compatibility with current delivery consumers (S3/HTTP webhooks).
- Add DB migration to capture the lowest-visible-timestamp per tenant required for closed-window semantics.

Out of scope: end-to-end UI changes for Console preview, long-term retention policy changes (addressed separately).
acceptance_criteria: Consistent CSVs: Running the same snapshot job twice for the same snapshot_id produces byte-identical CSVs and manifest entries.
Resumability: If export worker OOMs mid-run, restart picks up from last checkpoint and finishes without duplicating rows.
No cross-window leakage: Rows with event_time outside [window_start, window_end) are excluded.
Integration: S3 manifest and webhook payloads include snapshot_id and anchored_at and downstream consumers can detect partial vs final state.
Performance: Snapshot coordinator adds <5% overhead to average scheduled export latency at 95th percentile for small-medium tenants (<=10M rows).
tasks: Design snapshot manifest schema and open spec in docs/confluence: exports/atomic-snapshots (Maya)
Add DB field tenant_low_visible_ts and migration with backfill strategy (Liam)
Implement coordinator service with in-memory lease and Postgres-backed durable log (engineers: Liam, Priya)
Refactor CSV builder to accept checkpoint tokens and produce deterministic shard ordering (engineers: Omar)
Wire snapshot metadata into existing manifest generator and S3 uploader (engineers: Liam)
End-to-end tests with synthetic tenant data and deterministic timestamps (QA)
Canary rollout to internal staging tenants and run 72h validation comparing old vs snapshot flows (SRE)
Add observability: metric snapshot.duration, snapshot.checkpoints, snapshot.retries, and a dashboard tile (Observability)
Documentation: API notes for ad-hoc snapshot endpoint and webhook payload changes (Docs)
Post-deploy monitoring runbook and rollback criteria (Maya/Liam)
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, and QA. Agreed on anchoring model that uses tenant_low_visible_ts at snapshot start. Decided to use closed-open window semantics [t0, t1).

2025-02-12: Designed manifest spec draft (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/exports/atomic-snapshots) that includes snapshot_id (uuid), anchored_at (ISO8601), window_start, window_end, source_checkpoint (opaque token), status (partial|final).
2025-02-13: DB migration PR opened (github.com/redwood/console/pull/4821) to add tenant_low_visible_ts with online backfill using batched updates. Migration marked reversible.

2025-02-14: Implemented prototype coordinator service using Postgres advisory locks and a lightweight lease TTL. Prototype found race where two workers attempted overlapping partitions; added partition-range locking per tenant. PR opened (github.com/redwood/exports/pull/129).

2025-02-16: CSV builder refactor completed for checkpoint tokens and deterministic shard sort key. Unit tests added to assert idempotency. PR #131 linked. QA started building synthetic datasets for validation.

2025-02-18: Integration tests show deterministic outputs for 95% of synthetic cases. Observed a hanging edge case when checkpoint token expires during long-running export (>30m) — decision: extend checkpoint TTL to 2 hours and surface 'checkpoint_near_expiry' metric. Follow-up task created.
prs: github.com/redwood/exports/pull/129 - coordinator prototype and partition locking (in review)
github.com/redwood/exports/pull/131 - deterministic CSV builder and checkpoints (open)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stronger consistency (serializing writes during snapshot) would simplify deduplication but add latency; we chose partition-range leases to balance throughput and correctness.
We considered materializing a frozen export table for each snapshot but rejected due to storage cost for large tenants; instead we rely on checkpoint tokens and deterministic ordering.
Security note: snapshot manifests include no PII and all S3 URIs remain presigned as before. KMS usage unchanged.
runbook: If snapshot.jobs.error_rate > 1% for three consecutive runs, mark release as halted. To rollback, disable coordinator and revert to existing incremental run path via feature flag 'exports.atomic_snapshots' = false. Monitor snapshot.retries and snapshot.duration for anomalies. Notify PM and SRE.
